full_judgment:
11. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Advocate took us through the Notification being SRO No. 143 dated 10-6-2001. Notification being SRO No.172 dated 10-6-2004 and Notification being SRO No. 260 dated 30-8-2004.and submitted that in view of sub-section 2 of section 5 the petitioners as both commercial importer and trader have been paying VAT at the rate of 15% at the time of import and again at the same rate of 15% on the price of goods as approved by the VAT authorities at the trading stage and taking rebate under section 9 of the VAT Act, levy and collection of the advance VAT at the time of import of the goods was not applicable to the cases of the petitioners. 

 18. Thus empowered, National Board of Revenue issued the Notification being SRO No. 143-Law/2001/308-Musuk dated 7-6-2001 fixing the rate of value addition at 10 percent subject to certain terms and conditions for the purpose of payment of VAT at the rate of 1.5 percent by the traders (ব্যবসায়ী). Then, the National Board of Revenue issued the Notification being SRO No. 172-Law/2004/418-VAT dated 10-6-2004 superseding earlier Notification but maintaining said rate of value addition and fixing minimum VAT payable monthly/yearly by the retailers and others subject to certain conditions, The National Board of Revenue then issued the Notification being SRO No. 260-law/2004-431-VAT dated 30-8-2004 for payment in advance of said VAT of 1.5% what is payable at the trading or supply stage by the commercial importer at the time of import against the bill of entry on the assessable value plus customs duty, and supplementary duty and development surcharge, if any, plus value addition at the rate of 10 percent.
